auditor.notes: audit round 1 — before the revision loop

grounding.notes: round-1 grounding: confirmed the legacy CSV TODO in app/api/routes/legacy.py (F03) and the single lifespan hook in app/main.py (basis for the S3 seam claim)

findings.evidence: integration-plan.json e2e_gates v1 contained only E1 (submit-to-done) and E4 (unknown id); seams S2/S3 had no failure scenario — crash recovery (A3) and retry exhaustion (A4) had no E2E gate, so the two riskiest behaviors of the Stage would have closed on unit tests alone
findings.suggested_fix: add E2 (crash recovery: requeue, recompute exactly once, done) and E3 (retry exhaustion: failed, attempts 3, no 4th call) to e2e_gates; map them to acceptance A3/A4

findings.evidence: stage-contract.json v1 acceptance A6 description read 'status endpoint returns a meaningful progress value while running' — a third party could not judge PASS/FAIL ('meaningful' has no observable bound)
findings.suggested_fix: replace with 'returns HTTP 200 with status running and progress an integer in 0..100' + named test asserting the range

findings.evidence: stage-contract.json v1 out_of_scope did not name the legacy CSV export refactor even though input.md explicitly teases it — a named non-goal would have prevented the most likely scope-creep entry
findings.suggested_fix: add out_of_scope entry naming app/api/routes/legacy.py with reason
